solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Somewhat polite, rational, well-read types

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of something, so just a portion of the following words is taken

parts.note: run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Courteous, reasonable people who read a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are the educated, bookish class of society, people interested in literature.

clue.text: Rep pleased to upset shopkeepers

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over and throw its contents into disorder

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sales representative happily annoys the retailers he calls on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like part of the phrase 'pleased to upset' but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradespeople are those who run shops or trade in goods, so shopkeepers is a fair example-level synonym.

clue.text: Lead journalist travelled northbound carrying computers, etc.

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece sits inside the other
in a down clue, heading north means reading from the bottom up

parts.note: rode means travelled, past tense
IT, information technology, covers computers and the like

explanation.surface: The chief reporter went north with a laptop and other gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'computers, etc.' is a crossword favourite for the information technology abbreviation; 'Lead' is the adjective chief, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is the senior journalist in charge of a newspaper or section, leading the staff.

clue.text: Odd company in the outskirts of Sydney

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, between its edges
the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the city name
a crew is a group working together, a company

explanation.surface: A strange business located on the fringes of an Australian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwy is informal for strange or eccentric, so it means odd in the peculiar sense.

clue.text: Artist, extremely reclusive and seldom seen

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist

indicators.note: extremely here means at the extremes, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A painter who is very much a hermit and rarely appears in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' pretends to intensify reclusive; it actually trims the word to its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is uncommon, so it is seldom met with or observed.

clue.text: At times oddly lacking colour, like a wedding cake?

indicators.note: losing the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones in place

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the two words
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A cake that is sometimes strangely pale, as a wedding cake might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At times' reads as 'occasionally', but it is the source of the letters; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional wedding cake is built in stacked layers, each one a tier above the last.

clue.text: Fellow performer requiring money to be paid and all royalties up front

parts.note: a cost is the money something requires you to pay

indicators.note: up front points to the front of each word, so only initial letters are used

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An actor colleague who wants a fee plus all royalties paid in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up front' sounds like advance payment, but it selects the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star shares top billing with another actor, so is a fellow performer in the same production.

clue.text: Sis keen to act excited, getting access to lots of games?

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and agitated, so they fall into a new order

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sister eager to perform gets excited at the chance of attending many matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A season ticket admits the holder to every home fixture in a sporting season, many games for one price.

clue.text: Small, ultimately unwanted plant

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for small

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A little plant that, in the end, nobody wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwanted plant' reads as the definition of the whole, but unwanted only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed is a wild plant growing where it is not wanted, a specific kind of plant.

clue.text: Youngster ate green bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A child ate some unripe bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green bananas' reads as unripe fruit; bananas is the signal and green part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen, so a youngster.

clue.text: One observing a Serb spy in disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes how something looks, so the letters appear in a different form

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone watching a Serbian agent working undercover.
explanation.definitionFit: A passer-by is someone who happens to be walking past and so witnesses what happens.

clue.text: Computer programme starts to break out tasks

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words; the reversed run in 'to break' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Software that begins dividing up its jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bot, short for robot, is a program that carries out automated tasks.

clue.text: Individual touring clubs in days gone by

indicators.note: touring means going around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: one means a single individual
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A lone golfer who once travelled round the golf clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time in the past.

clue.text: Little wheel keeps turning up in box

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

parts.note: a caster is a small swivelling wheel on furniture

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A small wheel keeps appearing in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' at the end looks like a link word, but it is the word being turned and inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a round container, typically metal, used for storing things such as tea, so a box.

clue.text: Players complained loudly

indicators.note: loudly means spoken out, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: sighed, let out a weary breath of complaint

explanation.surface: The team members moaned noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team in sport, the group of players on one team.

clue.text: Beginning of con trick involving cunning

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick
art can mean craft or cunning

explanation.surface: The start of a swindle that requires guile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning of con' looks like a first-letter instruction; Beginning is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A starting point or starting position is the beginning, so the adjective matches Beginning used as a modifier.

clue.text: A flan's turned over, revealing layers

indicators.note: something turned over is upside down, so in a down entry the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a flan is a tart, so A + TART'S

explanation.surface: A dropped flan, upside down, exposing its layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata is the plural of stratum, horizontal layers such as rock beds.

clue.text: Tag on a couple of pages to finish

parts.note: taken as written
pp is the abbreviation for pages
to end is to finish

explanation.surface: Add a few pages to round off a document.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to attach or add something at the end, which is tagging it on.

clue.text: Nonsense about drink (gin)

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
to lap is to drink with the tongue
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: Rubbish talked over a glass of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink (gin)' reads as a drink named in brackets; gin is the snare, not the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, pretentious talk, which is rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Research centres set up in Govans, Baltimore

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so the letters read from the bottom
in here means contained within the following words, not built from pieces

parts.note: letters running across the two place names

explanation.surface: Science facilities established in a Baltimore neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Govans is a district of Baltimore, giving the surface its realism.
explanation.definitionFit: Labs, short for laboratories, are places where scientific research is carried out.

clue.text: Accountant given hush money

parts.note: CA is chartered accountant
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: An accountant receives a bribe to stay quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hush money' looks like one phrase meaning a bribe; it splits, with money the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is money in coins and notes, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A book in the post is missing

parts.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book
something in the post has been sent

explanation.surface: A posted book has gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means not present, so absent and missing are synonyms.

clue.text: Bothered dispensing with pounds, as required

indicators.note: dispensing with something means doing without it, so it is dropped

parts.note: needled means irritated or bothered
L, from Latin libra, stands for pounds

explanation.surface: Annoyed at having to do without the money, as was needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required both mean necessary, past participles of synonymous verbs.
